# Generated 2026-11-14 (UTC) by Tools/sky/build_sky_catalog.py; do not edit by hand, re-run the script instead.
# See DATA_SOURCES.md, section 'Night sky'.

# NASA data - every star position, magnitude and colour (S records, and the position and magnitude of N records):
#   Bright Star Catalogue, 5th Revised Ed. (Preliminary Version), Hoffleit D. & Warren W.H. Jr. 1991, Yale
#   University Observatory; served by NASA HEASARC as table heasarc_bsc5p (last modified 2022-02-03 22:57:23), public:
#     https://heasarc.gsfc.nasa.gov/W3Browse/star-catalog/bsc5p.html
#     https://heasarc.gsfc.nasa.gov/FTP/heasarc/dbase/tdat_files/heasarc_bsc5p.tdat.gz
#   input sha256 e2b2f8e9d615426f9478f88061235976143d49d8b25c6c15df3f3661c7095b53; 9110 rows, 14 without a position or magnitude
#   (the BSC's non-stellar placeholders: HR 92 95 182 1057 1841 2472 2496 3515 3671 6309 6515 7189 7539 8296), skipped.
#   Fields: ra/dec J2000 (FK5, epoch 2000), vmag (V), bv_color (B-V). No proper motion applied: the largest in
#   this file, HR 8085 (5.23 arcsec/yr), moves 3.1 arcmin by 2035.
#
# Not NASA data - the two declared exceptions:
#   1. The name text of N records: IAU Catalog of Star Names (IAU Division C WGSN), text version IAU-CSN,
#      last updated 2022-04-04, https://www.pas.rochester.edu/~emamajek/WGSN/IAU-CSN.txt
#      (official list: https://www.iau.org/public/themes/naming_stars/), released by the IAU under Creative Commons
#      Attribution; input sha256 84fac0c90f1b19abc491c2793469e0caa7b003ad1bc93a790ca41147010d0eb0.
#      Each name is matched to its BSC star by HR number (HD where the IAU designation is not an HR number).
#   2. C and L records: d3-celestial by Olaf Frohn, https://github.com/ofrohn/d3-celestial (data/ folder), BSD-3-Clause
#      (LICENSE reproduced at the end of this header): IAU constellation names, rank and label positions, and
#      stick figures after the IAU charts with line changes by O. Frohn; drawing conventions, not measurements.
#      Input files and their git blob ids, which identify the upstream revision:
#        constellations.json        632b8accc471d0220041273c4ab1c668a9fb4ce9
#        constellations.lines.json  ce64cf3c18b627f4d9749b9076cd4693b777697e
#        LICENSE                    bbf36e8a879754d582f40b9841123b8381cf5e93
#      Line endpoints are moved onto the nearest drawn BSC star within 0.1 deg (893 of 893 endpoints; largest move
#      30 arcsec); 0 have no BSC star that close and are kept as given.
#
# Frame: J2000 equatorial, degrees, RA in [0, 360). Numbers use the invariant format ('.' decimal point).
# One record per line; the name field is last and may contain spaces.
#   S <ra> <dec> <mag> <bv>      5080 stars, V <= 6.0, brightest first (B-V 0.65 where the BSC has none: 53)
#   N <ra> <dec> <mag> <name>     186 IAU proper names of stars with V <= 3.5, brightest first
#   C <ra> <dec> <rank> <name>     89 constellation label anchors for 88 constellations (one per part: Serpens
#                                     has two), IAU names, rank 1 (most prominent) .. 3, sorted by rank
#   L <ra1> <dec1> <ra2> <dec2>   743 constellation line segments
